summary: Pacific County lookout on Walville Peak: first used 1942, 40-foot tower 1955, destroyed by 1962 storm, removed by state 1968; half the site logged in 2015.

facts.design: 40-foot timber tower with a 14x14-foot live-in cab (1955); the register also describes an earlier 83-foot wooden tower with a 7x7-foot cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed by the state in 1968; about half the site was harvested in 2015

visit.trail_note: Reached by forest roads on state land; a trip report says a gate at the start is often open, especially in hunting season. A new road reaches the summit.

events.note: Oral Weese of Pe Ell reported in charge of the Walville lookout
Semi-permanent building, 10 feet square by 16 feet high, per a 1941 Washington Forest Fire Association report; Willhite dates a structure to 1941
Air Warning Service station activated March 9, 1942; the state kept the site when the service ended. Register: first used in 1942 with an 83-foot wooden tower
Fire near the lookout station in September 1951; about 1,000 acres per a newspaper, 1,800 acres per Willhite
40-foot timber tower with a 14x14-foot live-in cab; the register gives 1954 for a 40-foot live-in
Destroyed in the Columbus Day storm, October 12, 1962
Identical tower; sources give 1962 (register) or 1962-64 (state report)
Mrs. Roy Thompson of Lebam told a group in January 1966 that she had kept watch at the station for five years
Removed by the state; the trip report and firelookout.com say destroyed
About half the site harvested; the building site was not disturbed (trip report)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1954; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1955 biennial report and Willhite also says 1955. The story uses 1955 and gives the register's 1954.

The register says an 83-foot wooden tower was first used in 1942. The 1941 report quoted by Forest Lookouts describes a 10-by-16-foot building, and Willhite calls the tower possible. The story reports both.
The register and Forest Lookouts say removed by the state; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed. The story says removed and notes the other wording.
A newspaper estimate quoted by Forest Lookouts gives about 1,000 acres; Willhite gives 1,800 acres. The story gives both.
The register says the replacement came the same year (1962); the state report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 1962-64; Willhite's account is unclear. The story says early 1960s.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height of 12.2 m matches the 40-foot tower of 1955 to 1968. The register's first tower was 83 feet (about 25 m), so the story gives both. The register's coordinates (46.58845, -123.44309) match the brief, but the brief's other source (46.5895, -123.4175) was not read. The Willhite trip report says the 1955 tower may have been about a mile west at the Walville Peak summit, so the coordinates may refer to either site. The brief's access 'unknown' is left as is; the trip report describes state land with a gate that is often open. Willhite's 1962 replacement sentence is internally inconsistent, so the story says the timing is unclear.
